A tongue-in-cheek search for the real Book of God

Interestingly, the Book of Mormon does contain one thing that suggests that it might really be divinely inspired: The Parable of the Olive Tree. It stands out in the Book of Mormon, which is generally parable-light compared to the New Testament, and doesn't have an obvious parallel in the NT that it could have been copied from. Instead, it describes in substantial detail the exact process by which olive tree grafting would probably have taken place in the Mediterranean world two thousand years ago. It's extremely unlikely that Joseph Smith could have known the necessary history and botanical techniques, and the description is sufficiently detailed that it it is unlikely to have arisen by chance. This suggests that, at least in this one small area, Joseph Smith may actually have been divinely inspired. Of course, it's certainly not proof, and I wouldn't claim it is, but it certainly is a remarkable coincidence.
By the way, for those who are interested, the parable is in Chapter 5 of the Book of Jacob.
